newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea gold demand seen picking up on weak prices.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea gold demand seen picking up on weak prices.

text.p: South Korea's domestic gold demand is seen picking up this week on recent tumbling prices in world bullion markets, which also dampened lucrative smuggling business, traders in Seoul said on Tuesday.
"Domestic gold demand has recently been rising due to weak prices," a trader with Tong Yang Global said.
The Tong Yang trader said several trading houses were seen offering imported gold at prices lower than those for previously smuggled metal.
A trader with Ssangyong Corp said demand from the jewellery industry was also expected to grow as local buyers took advantage of lower international prices.
However, other traders said rising domestic demand was likely to be capped by lagging demand in summer plus the economic slowdown that followed a series of corporate collapses earlier this year.

Famine-striken North Korea's gold sales to its wealthier neighbour fell to $2.23 million (198 kg) in May from $19.81 million (1,727 kg) in the previous month, an official with the unification ministry said.
In late May traders said North Korea had sold a record amount of gold to the South in April to fund a lavish party to mark the birthday of the late "Great Leader" Kim Il-sung.
That came on top of gold sales by the North worth $9.3 million (811 kilos) in March.
"North Korea seemed to have shipped out a considerable amount of its bullion reserves in April," said a trade source close to the North Korean bullion trade.
The source added, "We have not heard any gold purchase by South Koreans in June. The North seemed to have put its gold sales on hold to raise its bullion reserves after large sell-off in April."
Last week, another bullion trader said North Korea had halted bullion sales to the South because of the third anniversary of the death of Kim Il-sung.

The daily selling price of domestic gold producer LG Metals for the precious metal, which is regarded as a benchmark for the local bullion wholesale market, fell on Tuesday to 9,600 won per gram from 9,910 won a week ago.
The company's silver price fell to 137 won per gram from 148 won a week earlier.
The telegraphic transfer selling rate for customers, posted by the Korea Exchange Bank, rose on Tuesday to 890.70 won against the dollar from 891.30 won a week earlier.
The rate is regarded as a benchmark of local foreign exchange rates for bullion companies.
